judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic is right: 3 > 2 (circle above square), 1 < 4 (rectangle left of diamond), 1 < 2 (oval below hexagon), 4 > 2 (hexagon right of square), the orderings 1, 2, 3 and 4, 3, 2, 1, and problem 8's two coordinates 3 > 1 and 3 > 2 all match verify.json and the key. The claim I cannot support is 'The single shelf diagram remains crisp and unambiguous across all references.' Problem 6 reads 'Go back to the shelf picture at the top of this page. On shelf 2, draw a small triangle in the empty space between the square and the hexagon.' Paging worksheet.pdf, the shelf figure is on page 1 and problem 6 is on page 3 -- the sentence tells a five-year-old the picture is on the page in front of them when it is two pages back, and the task requires drawing ON that figure. That is a genuine reference failure, not a nitpick, because the item cannot be completed on the page where it is printed. Separately, the judge scored answer_key_quality 4 while the delivered Quick Answers bank prints '1. -  2. -  3. -  5. -  6. -  8. -, -' -- six of eight rows, of which only row 6 is genuinely manual; the other dashes are verified relations dropped by render_quick_answers._fmt.

strengths_to_preserve: The answer key opens with 'The scene, in words. Shelf 3 (top): circle in spot 1, triangle in spot 3. Shelf 2 (middle): square in spot 2, hexagon in spot 4. Shelf 1 (bottom): rectangle in spot 1, oval in spot 2, diamond in spot 4' -- a textual restatement of the figure that lets a grader re-derive every answer without decoding the drawing, and that pins the figure/JSON agreement.

The directions fix the two coordinate conventions explicitly before any question uses them ('Shelf 1 is the bottom shelf. A shape on a bigger shelf number is higher up' / 'Spot 1 is farthest left'), which is what makes the numeric comparisons legitimate proxies for positional language.

Problem 8 is a genuine two-coordinate synthesis -- the triangle is compared to the oval on shelf AND spot -- and is the only item on the sheet that needs both position words at once, a sensible ramp endpoint for K-1.

root_causes.description: Nothing in the skill forbids page-relative deixis in problem prose, and nothing checks it after pagination. The author wrote 'at the top of this page' about a figure whose position is decided by LaTeX at compile time, and the figure landed two pages earlier.
evidence: worksheet.tex line 104: '\problem[6cm]{Go back to the shelf picture at the top of this page. On shelf 2, ...'
Paging worksheet.pdf: page 1 holds the shelf figure and problem 1; problem 6 is on page 3.
The item asks the child to draw on that figure, so the mismatch blocks completion rather than merely reading oddly.
gate_log.txt shows prose-ws PASS -- the prose gate compares numbers, not spatial references.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sends relation strings through bare sympify, which raises, and returns '---' -- the same glyph render_entry uses for manual-only problems. Six of eight rows in this key are dashes; only one is genuinely manual.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '1. -  2. -  3. -  5. -  6. -  8. -, -' with only '4. 1, 2, 3' and '7. 4, 3, 2, 1' printing values.
verify.json ids 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 are compare/relation entries that PASSED; id 6 is the only manual.
The key body does print the relations ('3>2', '1<4', '1<2'), so the answer exists and only the bank drops it.

root_causes.description: Each problem prints more response slots than its verify entries cover: the circle-a-word slots in problems 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8, and the shape-name slots in problems 4 and 7, have no entries.
evidence: Problem 4: 'Write the three shelf numbers in order ... Then write the name of the shape that is lowest and the name of the shape that is highest' -> one compare entry (asc [1,2,3]); the two names are unverified.
Problem 7: 'Write the four spot numbers in order ... Then write the name of the shape that is farthest right' -> one compare entry (desc [4,3,2,1]).
Problems 1, 2, 3, 5: 'Now circle the right word. The circle is above / below the square.' -> the positional word, which is the actual learning target, is never an expected.

improvements.title: Ban page-relative figure references and check figure/problem co-location after compile
improvements.proposed_change: State in SKILL.md that problem prose must not use pagination-dependent deixis ('this page', 'the picture above', 'at the top of the page') for a shared figure -- use a stable label ('the shelf picture on page 1') or reprint the figure with the problem. Add a post-compile check that maps each \problem and each shared figure to its PDF page (the machinery in tests/check_overprint.py already reads per-page geometry) and fails when a problem's text makes a same-page claim about a figure on another page. Any problem that asks the student to DRAW on a shared figure must reprint that figure inline.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem on page 3 contains 'at the top of this page' while the referenced tikz figure compiles onto page 1: the new gate must exit non-zero naming the problem and both page numbers. Today the fixture builds green (curr-048 did, with prose-ws PASS); after the fix it fails, and the variant that reprints the figure beside the problem passes.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a class of defect that makes an item literally uncompletable on the page it is printed on, which matters most for the youngest bands where a child cannot navigate back through a packet.
improvements.risk: Page-mapping problems to PDF pages needs the same segmentation the layout gate uses; a wrong mapping would produce false failures. Reprinting large figures costs page budget, which the compile-ss/compile-ws page checks must absorb.

improvements.title: Print the verified relation in the Quick Answers bank rather than a manual-review dash
improvements.proposed_change: Special-case relation strings in scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt before the sympify call and typeset them with the compared 'values' (e.g. '$3 > 2$'), and give manual-only rows a distinct marker so row 6 here is visually different from rows 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: a compare/relation entry must not render '---' and must include the relation; a manual entry must render a marker distinct from every verified row. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Six of eight rows in this key regain content, and the one genuinely manual row becomes identifiable.
improvements.risk: Wider entries can force a narrower column layout in the bank; re-check answer-key page counts.

improvements.title: Cover the positional word and shape-name slots, not only the numeric comparison
improvements.proposed_change: Move the coverage rule in SKILL.md from per-problem-id to per-rendered-answer-slot and enforce it in tests/check_layout.py. On this sheet that means an entry for each 'circle the right word' choice (above/below, left/right) -- expressible as a read_data lookup over the scene dictionary the key already states in words -- and entries for the lowest/highest/farthest-right shape names in problems 4 and 7.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture problem printing an ordering slot plus two name slots with a single compare entry: check_layout must exit non-zero. Passes today (problems 4 and 7 here); fails after the fix until the entries are added.
improvements.expected_impact: The positional vocabulary that is the actual standard being taught (K.G / 1.G position words) becomes verified rather than inferred from a numeric proxy.
improvements.risk: Encoding word answers needs a lookup type the authors must use consistently; over-eager slot counting could flag decorative rules.

case_summary: A well-conceived scene worksheet: one shelf diagram, two clearly stated coordinate conventions, and a ramp from single-axis comparisons to a two-coordinate description, with problem 6 correctly flagged manual. All eight numeric results are correct. Three defects sit behind the 32/32. Problem 6 tells the child the shelf picture is 'at the top of this page' when it is two pages back and then asks them to draw on it, so the item cannot be done where it is printed. The Quick Answers bank prints six dashes of which only one is genuinely manual. And the sheet's actual learning target -- the positional word circled in problems 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and the shape names in 4 and 7 -- is never machine-checked; only the numeric proxy is.
